text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 2 in history.
1547 - Hernando Cortes, Spanish conqueror of Mexico, died; he fought and conquered Mexico and in 1522 became governor and captain-general of "New Spain".
1697 - The choir in St Paul's Cathedral, virtually destroyed after the Civil War and repaired and redesigned by Sir Christopher Wren, was formally opened for worship.
1723 - Philippe Duc D'Orleans died; he had been appointed regent of France for the young Louis XV in 1715.
1804 - Napoleon Bonaparte was crowned Emperor of France in Paris by Pope Pius VII.
1805 - Napoleon won a brilliant victory at the battle of Austerlitz, known as the "Battle of the Three Emperors", against Russia and Austria.
1814 - The Comte de Sade, known as the Marquis de Sade, died; his unnatural sexual practices and writings about them led to the term "sadism".
1823 - U.S. President James Monroe introduced his "Monroe Doctrine" under which it was held that the American continents were not to open to future colonisation by any European power.
1852 - In France, the Second Empire was proclaimed with Napoleon III as emperor.
1859 - American anti-slavery campaigner John Brown was hanged after an abortive raid on the federal arsenal in Virginia.
1859 - French artist Georges Seurat born; founder of the school of neo-impressionism, he also developed the technique of pointillism.
1899 - British conductor John Barbirolli born; he conducted the New York Philharmonic and the Halle Orchestra in Manchester.
1901 - King Camp Gillette patented the first safety razor which had a double-edged disposable blade.
1942 - The world's first nuclear chain reaction took place at the University of Chicago when physicists led by Enrico Fermi created a chain reaction.
1954 - Senator Joseph McCarthy was condemned by the U.S. Senate for misconduct after his ruthless investigations of thousands of suspected communists.
1966 - British Prime Minister Harold Wilson met Rhodesian leader Ian Smith to discuss the dispute over Rhodesian independence.
1971 - The United Arab Emirates was proclaimed.
1971 - The unmanned Soviet spacecraft Mars 3 landed on Mars.
1972 - A general election in Australia resulted in a Labour victory, the first since 1949; Gough Whitlam became prime minister.
1975 - In the Netherlands, six Moluccan guerrillas hijacked a train at Beilin and held passengers and crew hostage killing three.
1979 - In Iran, electors voted overwhelmingly in favour of a new constitution giving absolute power to Ayatollah Khomeini.
1982 - The first permanent artificial heart was implanted in Barney Clark, a Seattle dentist, by Dr William De Vries at the University of Utah.
1990 - After German reunification, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition of CDU/CSU and FDP won Germany's first free all-German elections since 1932.
1991 - Joseph Cicippio, U.S. hostage in Lebanon, was released after being held since September 1986.
1993 - Pablo Escobar, boss of the Medellin cocaine cartel in Colombia, was killed in a shootout as police tried to arrest him.
